paragraphs.text: David, when persecuted by Saul, prayed this way, leaving the same to the Church as a monument, how to seek relief against their miseries.
paragraphs.label: a

paragraphs.text: I am not an enemy to them, but I pity them even though they are cruel to me.
paragraphs.label: b

paragraphs.text: Which was a fair token that he believed that God would deliver him.
paragraphs.label: c

paragraphs.text: He confesses that God is good to all but only merciful to poor sinners.
paragraphs.label: d

paragraphs.text: By crying and calling continually he shows how we must not be weary, even though God does not immediately grant our request but that we must earnestly and often call on him.
paragraphs.label: e
paragraphs.anchor: attend to the voice of my

paragraphs.text: He condemns all idols as they can do nothing to declare that they are gods.
paragraphs.label: f
paragraphs.anchor: are there any works like unto

paragraphs.text: This proves that David prayed in the Name of Christ the Messiah of whose kingdom he here prophecies.
paragraphs.label: g

paragraphs.text: He confesses himself ignorant till God has taught him, and his heart variable and separate from God, till God join it to him, and confirm it in his obedience.
paragraphs.label: h

paragraphs.text: That is, from most great danger of death: out of which none but the almighty hand of God could deliver him.
paragraphs.label: i

paragraphs.text: He shows that there can be no moderation or equity where proud tyrants reign, and that the lack of God's fear is as a privilege to all vice and cruelty.
paragraphs.label: k

paragraphs.text: He boasts not of his own virtues, but confesses that God of his free goodness has always been merciful to him, and given him power against his enemies, as to one of his own household.
paragraphs.label: l
